title: No source publishes the rwb-case case state read or the case-move answer the pricing step consumes
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 13, 19, 41); _work/msr/context/S5.md (connection matrix, Ownership Map rows of S5); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T-A.1)
section: s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 2 and 8; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13 Solution plan
description: The pricing step reads the case state and answers three case moves, and no source document publishes either operation. TSD S5 T-A.1 lists this service own operations only, and the connection matrix of slide 13 gives rwb-asset Temporal to rwb-decision and Temporal and events to rwb-payment and rwb-partner, with no REST row to rwb-case. The story therefore builds against the documented use and a placeholder, and the case-move answer is read on the workflow boundary as the stage outcome the parent CaseWorkflow applies.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 13 row S5 Asset gives T to P7 and T E to P8 and S9 and no cell for P3; slide 19 IN lists the four consumed events and names no case operation; TSD S5 T-A.1 carries API-S5-001 to API-S5-005 only, and T5.2 says calls go through the published Java interfaces of P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 without naming one.
proposed: rwb-case publishes the case state read and the case-move operation, or confirms the stage-outcome signal as the only boundary, before the wave 2 tag; RWB-S5-E3028-CON replaces the placeholder with the published name in a minor version.

title: No source publishes the pricing proposal of rwb-agent or the asset and COLLINS fact the price is computed from, and the connection matrix carries no arrow for either
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-28); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.11 integration points); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slide 13, slides 19 and 41); _work/msr/context/S5.md
section: s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 3, 4 and 5; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes
description: R-DIS-28 has the pricing agent propose the opening price and the floor as the reserve and names the Agent Runtime and COLLINS as its systems, and the FSD reads the COLLINS economics from the ACE view v_ace_score. In the target the agent is rwb-agent (P10), the ACE views are rwb-source-data own (P1) and DP-05 forbids this service to read them, but no source publishes the proposal operation or the asset and COLLINS fact, and the connection matrix of slide 13 carries no arrow from P10 or P1 to S5. The story therefore requests the proposal and reads the fact on their owners contracts with a placeholder, and the call type is carried as an assumption.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-28 systems column reads Agent Runtime, COLLINS; FSD S5 A2.11 integration points read Workbench, ACE (COLLINS scores ingested by ACE; v_ace_score); Architecture v5 slide 13 row S5 Asset has no cell for P10 or P1 and the legend gives T, N, R, E, S and F only; the Ownership Map S5 rows carry no agent or source-data operation.
owner_role: P10 rwb-agent owner, P1 rwb-source-data owner
proposed: rwb-agent publishes the proposal operation with its model reference and rwb-source-data publishes the asset and COLLINS fact, or the architecture states the call type (REST, event or Temporal activity); RWB-S5-E3028-CON replaces the placeholders in a minor version.

title: R-DIS-17 updates the appraised value, no column of rwb_asset holds it and the appraisal belongs to rwb-valuation
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1 asset and listing, T-A.1 API-S5-003); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.11, A2.9); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-17); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slide 42 notes)
section: s7 Acceptance criteria note on AC3; s8 BR3; s9 State transitions; s11 Data; s13 Database and migrations
description: Legacy AC3 and R-DIS-17 say the step updates the appraised value and resets the list and floor price inputs. The target has no appraised value column in asset, listing or asset_sale, and POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations is rwb-valuation own operation under the Ownership Map ruling ASM-A6-api-6, while the connection matrix of slide 13 carries no S5 to S1 arrow. The story therefore reads the value from rwb-valuation and treats the update as the reset of its own price inputs, and it writes no appraisal value.
evidence: TSD S5 T3.1 lists asset, listing and asset_sale with no appraised value column; TSD S5 T-A.1 carries API-S5-003 POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations; R-DIS-17 action column reads Update the appraised value and reset the list and floor price inputs; Architecture v5 slide 13 row S5 Asset has no cell for S1.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset data owner with S1 rwb-valuation owner
proposed: The S1 owner publishes the appraisal read and the S5 data owner confirms whether a copy of the appraised value is needed on the listing row; the DB story adds the column in its own Flyway sequence only if it is confirmed.

title: The floor percentage and the approval limit of VR-S5-011-1 have no value and no owner row in the sources
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.11.3.1 VR-S5-011-1); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-29); _work/msr/context/S5.md (Temporal and Drools slides 12 and 13, Approval (DoA)), legacy message MSG-S5-001
section: s4 Flow step 10; s5 X5; s8 BR6 and BR9; s13 Configuration and reference data; s14 Validation and messages
description: VR-S5-011-1 refuses a floor below the approver limit and MSG-S5-001 carries the two placeholders pct and limit, but no source gives either value, names the level that holds a limit or says where the limit is stored. The kit approval takes the delegation-of-authority lookup as a parameter and the delegated-authority rows are rwb-access (P4) facts read at their version, so this story asks for the values and writes none.
evidence: FSD S5 A2.11.3.1 gives VR-S5-011-1 and MSG-S5-001 with {pct} and {limit} and no value; R-DIS-29 condition reads officer_approved = Y and names no limit; Temporal and Drools Design slide 12 describes Approval (DoA) with the DoA lookup as a parameter; the S5 context pack carries no authority table.
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision rule owner, P4 rwb-access delegated-authority owner
proposed: The P4 owner confirms the delegated-authority table and the P7 owner places the percentage and the limit in the DISPOSAL package at its next version, with the version recorded in the decision record.

title: The approval child workflow of the floor is not published, and the sources do not say how the head of NPA role is bound to the approval
source: _work/msr/context/S5.md (Temporal and Drools Design slides 12 and 13); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slide 41); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T6.1); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.11.3.3)
section: s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 11; s7 Acceptance criteria note on AC1; s8 BR6; s12.2 REST operations consumed
description: AC1 requires the head of NPA to approve the floor and the kit provides the approval child workflow on rwb-decision, but no source publishes the element names of that request or the shape of its answer, and the TSD T6.1 matrix gives RW-HEADNPA the right RA on Asset and disposal without an approval right of its own. The story requests the approval with the case, the asset, the floor and the officer proposal and stores only the returned reference, and it records the role binding as an assumption.
evidence: Temporal and Drools Design slide 12 lists the Approval (DoA) kit template with no interface; slide 13 notes place ApprovalWorkflow from the kit on rwb-decision; TSD S5 T6.1 gives RW-HEADNPA RA; FSD S5 A2.11.3.3 lists Head of NPA as also users only.
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner, P4 rwb-access owner
proposed: The P7 owner publishes the approval child workflow request and answer elements and the P4 owner confirms that RW-HEADNPA is the role the floor approval asks for; RWB-S5-E3028-CON replaces the placeholder in a minor version.

title: The channel and status values of this step, the step schedule by asset class and two legacy screen states have no value or list in the sources
source: Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.2 lists of values); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.11); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-29); legacy RWB-E3-028 screen table (SCR-23)
section: s4 Flow steps 7 and 13; s9 State transitions; s11 Data; s13 Configuration and reference data
description: The listing row carries a sale channel and a status and R-DIS-29 sets the step schedule by asset class, but LOV-SALE-CHANNEL and LOV-LISTING carry no value for a priced or reserved listing, no source lists the step schedule, and the legacy screen states below limit and published are screen states and not list values. The step therefore reads the values at their version and carries the placeholder, and it adds no enumeration member.
evidence: TSD S5 T3.2 gives LOV-SALE-CHANNEL as DUTCH_AUCTION, BROKER, DIRECT, LED_AUCTION and RAMC and LOV-LISTING as DRAFT, LIVE, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD and WITHDRAWN; R-DIS-29 action column reads Fix the floor as the reserve and set the step schedule by asset class; the legacy screen table gives SCR-23 the states Draft, below limit, approved and published; no list of step schedules appears in the TSD.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset data owner, P7 rwb-decision rule owner
proposed: The S5 data owner confirms the channel and status values the pricing step uses and the P7 owner publishes the step schedule per asset class as reference data of the DISPOSAL package; the two screen states are mapped to the published list values.

title: The split plan carries no requirement id for this slice
source: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (slice rows of RWB-S5-E3028-APP and RWB-S5-E3028-CON); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.11, requirements served REQ-S5-004); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (FEAT-AST-11)
section: s2 Business rationale; s18 Traceability requirement table
description: The story serves FEAT-AST-11 of the FSD module S5 and REQ-S5-004 of its requirements served, and the split plan requirement rows for this slice are empty, so the traceability table states the requirement from the module and cites this gap instead of an invented REQ id.
evidence: The plan slice rows for RWB-S5-E3028-APP and RWB-S5-E3028-CON carry reqs as an empty list; FSD S5 requirements served states REQ-S5-004; the Epics 3 to 8 Specification names FEAT-AST-11 without a requirement id.
proposed: The requirement owner allocates a requirement id for the slice at the next plan revision and the traceability row is repointed without a story change.

title: The price model, its version and the reserve basis of R-DIS-28 are not specified and no service owns the model
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-28); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.11 integration points); legacy RWB-E3-028 data table (v_ace_score model_code and model_version)
section: s2 Business rationale; s4 Flow step 4; s12.8 Contract fakes; s19 Out of scope
description: R-DIS-28 has the pricing agent propose the floor as the reserve, and the legacy data table reads the COLLINS model code and model version from v_ace_score, but no source defines the reserve basis, names the model that proposes the price or says which service owns it in the target. The story reads the model reference and its version from the agents answer and records them in the decision record, and it computes no proposal and fixes no reserve basis.
evidence: R-DIS-28 action column reads Pricing agent proposes the opening price and the floor price as the reserve and its systems are Agent Runtime and COLLINS; the legacy Data table lists v_ace_score with model_code, model_version and estimate_value under DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279; no target document names a price model owner.
owner_role: P10 rwb-agent owner, P7 rwb-decision model risk owner
proposed: The P10 owner publishes the model reference and its version in the proposal and the model risk owner records the reserve basis with the model governance documents.

title: The asset table is absent from the Ownership Map table list for S5
source: _work/msr/context/S5.md (ownership rows owned by S5: tables listing and asset_sale only); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1 asset); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 19 and 41)
section: s3 Preconditions; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s13 Database and migrations
description: The pricing step reads the asset for its reference, its asset class and its book value, and TSD S5 T3.1 defines the asset row, but the Ownership Map table list of S5 carries listing and asset_sale only, so the asset row has no owner row in the map. The story reads the row as S5 own, from the service row of the architecture and the module TSD, and records the absence instead of declaring another owner.
evidence: The S5 context pack lists the S5 tables as asset_sale and listing; TSD S5 T3.1 defines asset with DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042 and T3.3 gives its relationships; Architecture v5 slides 19 and 41 place assets and their holding with S5.
owner_role: Ownership Map owner, S5 rwb-asset data owner
proposed: The Ownership Map adds the asset row with owner S5 at its next version and the DB story of the service creates the table in schema rwb_asset.
